speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what are the employability support given to help workers manage structural changes like digital disruption.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower as Singapore transits to an endemic COVID-19 economy, what are the plans to help our workforce as well as Singapore companies to shift their plans and strategies to meet the changes when the economy opens up gradually.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what is the Ministry’s assessment on the effectiveness of job placement and training support that are currently provided to assist unemployed and under-employed workers, especially those who are in distressed sectors and those who are facing headwinds during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry intends to introduce additional measures to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of prevailing national guidelines especially for industries such as the food and beverage and the construction sectors.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether studies have been done by the Ministry to understand the digital preparedness of our workers aged 40 to 60 years; and (b) what are the support measures put in place to enable digitally-disadvantaged workers to take on job roles which have pivoted into the digital space.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On employment	outcomes and support for workers, I hope to give a more holistic reply.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On the whole, the labour market continued its gradual recovery in the first half of 2021.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Although the ratio of job vacancies to unemployed persons reached a high of 1.63 in June 2021 – we have got very, very high job vacancies relative to unemployed persons – however, many of these openings were in the construction sector where the shortage has been due to public health border measures.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There were also pockets of recovery in other sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, resident employment grew and unemployment continued to ease.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, the labour market has clearly not fully recovered.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Therefore, we must remain vigilant, maintain our support measures for affected workers and we will continue to leave no stone unturned in helping all locals who need our support.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In particular, the $2.2 billion SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package has helped to cushion the impact of COVID-19 on the labour market since its launch in April last year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The supported jobseekers reflect the profile of our workforce.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Close to six in 10 placements into jobs and skills opportunities went to mid-career PMETs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Workforce Singapore (WSG) saw a large increase in placements through Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs) with more than 14,000 locals supported.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: WSG and NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) expanded their service touch points, with 24 new SGUnited Jobs and Skills Centres established islandwide, in every HDB town.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have also appointed Adecco as the first SGUnited Placement Partner, to offer another avenue for mature workers aged 40 and above, long-term unemployed jobseekers, or persons with disabilities, to access professional career matching services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Close to 44,000 jobseekers found jobs through these career matching services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Dr Tan Yia Swam, Mr Edward Chia and Mr Sharael Taha were concerned about workers being displaced from distressed sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are supporting such workers through a variety of ways.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The first and most important priority is to save jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is helping companies preserve their workforce's skills and competencies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are continually recalibrating our support based on each sector's specific needs and recovery trajectory.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The most-affected sectors such as F&B services, retail and hotels have rolled out Job Redesign Reskilling programmes with WSG's assistance.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They are using the downtime to train and to upskill existing workers to take on redesigned and enhanced job roles as part of their industry transformation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have reskilled and redeployed close to 9,000 workers through these programmes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Second, we stand ready to support some of the workers who may have to leave their jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The number of retrenchments rose to about 26,000 in 2020, although the incidence of retrenchment remained lower than past recessionary years.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is comparable to levels seen in 2018 and 2019.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Notwithstanding Phase Two (Heightened Alert) earlier this year, affected sectors such as F&B services, retail trade and arts, entertainment and recreation did not see elevated retrenchments as more employers put workers on short work-week or temporary lay-offs instead.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Amongst all retrenched residents, the six-month re-entry rate was 64.4% in the second quarter of 2021.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is an improvement from 61.6% in 2020.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is also comparable to pre-COVID-19 re-entry rates in 2018 and 2019.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The tripartite Retrenchment Taskforce follows up with every notified retrenchment by proactively reaching out to the affected workers and offering them employment assistance.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This includes providing information kits on career resources, briefings on available employment facilitation and one-on-one coaching by WSG and NTUC-e2i's career coaches.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Third, we encourage companies who need workers to create jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We provide the Jobs Growth Incentive (JGI) to support employers expand local hiring.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Four in 10 were in growth sectors such as wholesale trade, professional services and information and communications, while one in five were in the recovering F&B services and retail sectors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Encouragingly, half of the JGI-supported hires were not employed at the point of hire and six in 10 – I think this is in reference to the hon Member of Parliament Jessica Tan's earlier question – earned the same or higher pay compared to their last drawn.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I also recently announced the extension of the JGI to March 2022 to secure the labour market recovery and to support our local jobseekers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: JGI provides additional support when employers hire mature workers, persons with disabilities as well as ex-offenders.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Each of such hires could attract up to $36,000 of JGI support.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I strongly encourage and urge all of our companies looking to recruit to not delay their plans and bring forward their hires.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about support for senior workers to stay in their current jobs or to pivot to new jobs in other industries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We should be encouraged by the resilience of our senior workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I will not go over the details a second time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think all of you would have gotten the handout earlier as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also asked about platform workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Platform workers are a diverse group and we are very committed to supporting them in their plans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many, in a feedback survey to us, tell us that they prefer such work because of the flexibility and the autonomy it affords.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For them, we have recently established an Advisory Committee on Platform Workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This committee will consult widely and examine, get feedback from the industry to see how they can be better supported.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For those looking to transit to regular employment, WSG and NTUC's e2i offer career matching services, including career coaching, employability workshops and job fairs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For example, in 2021, NTUC's e2i conducted several career re-invention workshops in collaboration with the National Private Hire Vehicles Association and NTUC LearningHub to help platform drivers explore new career pathways.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In addition, digital services like the MyCareersFuture (MCF) portal can be accessed at all hours of the day.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The whole range of SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package support is also available to them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We know that it is challenging for platform workers to transit to regular employment but WSG will continue to put in its best effort to support them in their job search.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ms Hany Soh, Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about how jobseekers are matched to job vacancies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It would not be possible to match all job vacancies with jobseekers perfectly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We understand and we appreciate this and more so especially when we or our loved ones are looking for a job.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It always helps to have as wide an option base as possible and to choose the best option that is available.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But if vacancies are accumulating and they are left unfilled, it also indicates that the labour market is having difficulty in accessing and finding the right talent to fill these vacancies, and businesses have to continue to run.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is actually down slightly from the pre-COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In September, I set up the Jobs Taskforce to coordinate efforts across key Government agencies to enable more locals to take up in-demand jobs with good wages and prospects in key sectors of our economy such as financial services and info-communications and technology.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Jobs Taskforce will work with tripartite partners and employers to make and enable the labour market to function even better.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Some vacancies take longer to fill because the wage or working conditions may not be as attractive as other options available to jobseekers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If they remain persistently unfilled, businesses may have to redesign the job roles.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They may even have to review their strategies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: WSG offers job redesign support under the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG-JR), which was launched in December 2020.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Through PSG-JR, enterprises can receive support to work with pre-approved job redesign consultants to redesign their work processes, their tasks and their responsibilities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We welcome all enterprises to come on board to troubleshoot any difficulties they may face in hiring new workers and grow their businesses, especially in our Singapore Core.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Other vacancies may persist because the employer is hoping to get someone who is already fully trained and ready to jump straight into the job from day one.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are helping employers to go beyond the "plug-and-play" mindset and approach by supporting Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Employers who have adopted this approach have found that people recruited through CCPs are a good fit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our industries are digitalising rapidly and as pointed out by Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Edward Chia, digital competencies are very highly sought after.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng has asked about the number of workers who have been given employment assistance to cope with digital disruption.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As digitalisation accelerates, it has affected jobs to varying degrees.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, many jobs would require workers to acquire basic digital literacy skills such as learning how to use digital communication platforms to market a product.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Second, some jobs will require workers to learn how to implement digital technology such as robotic process automation to automate processes or to perform more complex analysis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Third, there will be growing demand for deep technology skills, which will bring us into the next bound of digital transformation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many workers in the first category will make this transition seamlessly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, we work with unions, Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs), companies and education institutions to scaffold their learning.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Under the SME Digital Reboot programme, Ngee Ann Polytechnic and NTUC LearningHub will work with 500 SMEs to provide workers with training in areas such as digital marketing and digital communication.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) also drives digital adoption among vulnerable segments under the SG Digital Office while the National Library Board runs a range of digital readiness programmes on digital work skills, competencies and emerging technologies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Moving on to the second category, where we will see more workers becoming implementers of digital technology.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is already happening rapidly in sectors such as logistics and manufacturing, where digital technology is embedded in the physical world, or what we term as Industry 4.0.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we hope that by the third quarter, we will have 300 companies onboarding the IHCI.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Parallel to this effort, the unions and employers have also established more than 600 company training committees (CTCs) where they work closely together to drive business and workforce transformation, including in digital competencies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The third category of jobs, where deep technology skills are required, is also where we see some of the highest demand across the economy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Locals placed through TeSA have taken on jobs, such as Systems Analysts or Data Scientists, across sectors including Information and Communications, Financial Services, Professional Services, Manufacturing and Wholesale Trade and Retail.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The JTMs are detailed sectoral manpower studies that map out the impact of technology and digitalisation on individual jobs over the medium term.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, I am confident that with the Government and tripartite partners continuing to work closely and just as importantly, with your concerns, with your collective efforts, we will be able to help our businesses and workers to emerge stronger together.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is important that our workforce is equipped with the necessary skillsets to deal with the structural changes in our economy, post-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How does the Ministry check whether these training and employment assistance are fit for purpose, ensuring that there are right workers equipped with the right skills in the right sectors?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And what will be the KPIs for tracking outcomes for success?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My second supplementary question pertains to Question No 12.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In terms of plans and strategies for our workforce and companies, can the Ministry share in greater details: (a) what is insufficient today and what must change; (b) what must our workforce and companies aspire to do; and (c) when these plans must be firmed up to prepare for the opening of our economy?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Doing so will help to ensure that our workers have the necessary skillsets to take on good jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In addition, under my other portfolio in MTI, through EDB, through ESG, we have got various market readiness grants.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There is also the global innovation alliance network, with the global connect network that we work very closely with SBF, to try to see the needs, the industry trends in many of the developed countries all over the world and to see how we can continue to keep our local workforce abreast of changes to keep them ahead and to keep them competitively sharp.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that answers the Member's first question.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the Member's second point about plans and strategies for our workforce and companies, indeed, this pandemic has accelerated disruption and transformation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It has highlighted very clearly the need for businesses to strengthen their resilience as well as to have to constantly think about the disruptive changes that will come and to diversify.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This would not just apply to business transformation but also to the workforce transformation as well, to keep our workers adept, to keep them agile and nimble.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, emerging trends today that we can see, such as automation and digitalisation, have radically transformed and changed the way we work, with remote work becoming more prevalent across many workplaces.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To retain our competitive advantage, to find good sustainable jobs for Singaporeans, our efforts to continue to transform and innovate our economy must continue so that we can strengthen, fortify our business environment and we can ensure that Singapore always remains the preferred hub, the preferred location for trade, for investment, particularly in new emerging growth areas, for instance, like additive manufacturing in Fintech.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The anchoring of global companies which meet our desired profile and the aspirations of Singaporeans will help to preserve, spur the creation of good jobs, strengthen our Singapore Core.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think that point that we debated so long yesterday adds to the fact that we must continue to reinforce trust, reinforce the credibility, our reputation that other economies have, the faith and trust, in us through the years and, hopefully, through the decades ahead.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the same time, we are also looking to build up our CET pipeline ahead of demand in key growth areas in the green economy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many of these initiatives come, they converge, we distill them and we develop a very targeted approach to help our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many of my middle-aged residents have faced difficulties traversing the new digital normal.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And many have admitted they are left behind in Singapore's drive to be digital.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many are unable to use with confidence online applications, even such as simple ones like Singpass online or even download an e-copy of their CPF, much less so becoming overnight digital marketeers or social media influences.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: My residents have told me their frustrations after taking classes and courses, their employers have told them that those classes are irrelevant to the job roles that they are seeking.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Will the Ministry consider working with companies then on identifying key digital skills and the appropriate courses, perhaps across the many different skillsets, on the SkillsFuture platform, that will allow our less digitally inclined workers to be on a level playing field with digital natives in the hiring process and in future in job promotions?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the training part, in terms of the elderly residents, we do have SG Digital Ambassadors to go around to teach them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And for those, even with the literacy skills, the National Library Board (NLB) also has a whole slew of programmes to help them transform as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But I think what the Member has hit on is a key issue which is really making sure that when companies and the workforce innovate, when they digitalise and so on, they must be relevant to the needs of the company.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To that end, that is really a huge drive by WSG to develop these Career Conversion Programmes, because they are working with the company.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, NTUC has the CTCs, again working with the companies to understand the needs and to see how we can help to redesign, if the jobs need to be redesigned, or to help to train our local workforce, our Singaporean Core to be adept and to be able to fit into the expectations of the company.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Beyond that, I have shared earlier on that I have formed the Jobs Taskforce to understand where the gaps are, when there is an inability to clear that match.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, there are multiple initiatives at different levels to try to reach out to as many Singaporeans as possible.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As there will always be laggard effect in reskilling, what is the Minister's assessment of the potential structural impact on the labour market, should job vacancies remain elevated?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That is what keeps all of us in the Manpower Ministry and also, I believe – Minister Chan is here – MOE up on our toes all the time in working and identifying.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we prioritise, ensuring that the training, the upskilling and the reskilling of our Singaporean Core remains on track, so that we minimise the lag.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Contemporaneously, we also, through our global network of the innovation alliances and so on, see what lies ahead and how do we even prep our workforce to stay ahead of the curve all the time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the rest who do experience that lag, in terms of the hiring, we do have a number of initiatives and programmes that we roll out to help them to catch up and also, to ensure that they are able to keep up in terms of the pivoting.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If I were to go into the details of each one of the schemes, it probably will take us another session.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But suffice to say that there are a whole slew of programmes available that today, we are already seeing quite a lot of traction.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, those are the things that we are looking into as well.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I understand from the Minister's response earlier that about 57% of the job vacancies have continued to be left unfilled after six months.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, I wish to find out whether options, such as the Career Trials or Place-and-Train programmes, had ever been explored by the employers with these job vacancies.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If yes, whether there have been any findings on why such initiatives were unsuccessful in filling these job vacancies.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If the answer is no, do we actually know the reasons behind why there is a reluctance from these companies in considering the adoptions of such job placement programmes?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There will always be a certain level of job vacancies in a properly functioning labour market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Sometimes, the job vacancies could just be due to a skills mismatch where the jobseekers may not have the full set of requisite skills to be ready for the job.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, as I have shared, this is where the Career Conversion Programmes come in.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We work with the companies to develop these Company Training Committees to ensure that the jobseekers have a proper market-clearing opportunity for them to be able to match up to the expectations of the employers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many of the employers who have actually worked with us to adopt this approach, have found out that the people whom they hire and even then the middle-aged workers, because of their experiential wisdom, the aptitude and attitude, they have actually found that after that conversion programme, that upskilling and reskilling, they found that they actually become pretty good fit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we can see that these programmes that we have put up, we are beginning to see quite good traction.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We need to let it run a bit more because you need to give it that runway before it tapers off or it plateaus off, then we can either reinforce or pivot to a new programme to build upon it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are still employers who would just prefer a "plug-and-play"; ostensibly, because some of them are in very high growth, and they keep getting new business coming in all the time, they have no time to think about training you and having that so-called comfort zone and that spare capacity of bandwidth to train.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But we encourage these employers to fundamentally adopt some form of a mindset change as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the people who are coming on to be trained, for them, that confidence in themselves, the adaptability is also fundamentally important, because it takes two hands to clap.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Through the Member's questions, it is obvious that she has thought through this very carefully.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If I may borrow or leverage the Member's question, if I can leverage everyone here, it would be to reach out to all of the communities, the employers, the businesses and so on, to fundamentally change their mindset where they can be a lot more forgiving in their hiring.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Different people have different skillsets that even though it may not necessarily fill that immediate job role, but if the company has that latitude, you will be able to find something for that Singaporean employee.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Notice of Motion.

text: Question Nos 18-19 and 47 have been postponed to the next available sitting of Parliament.]
